key_insight: Agreement near equilibrium does not guarantee reliable fatigue predictions: NequIP’s much lower stacking fault energy produces far more plastic deformation than EAM.
engineering_relevance: Interatomic potentials used for fatigue and fracture simulations need validation under cyclic loading, not just against near-equilibrium properties.
method: Compare EAM and foundational NequIP potentials on static and emergent properties.
Apply fatigue cycling to a nanoscale flaw modeled after the Griffith crack problem.
Analyze per-atom energy distributions after loading.
evidence_signal: Both potentials closely match reference data for many near-equilibrium properties, but NequIP predicts an intrinsic stacking fault energy about seven times lower than EAM, with the largest post-loading differences at thermally inaccessible energies.
watch_item: Without direct experimental validation, comparison with EAM is not definitive; memory-related crashes and silent extrapolation also warrant caution.
paper_title: Emergent Fatigue Dynamics from Foundational Interatomic Potentials
